SessionWriter integration for HABRO ADB
======================================

Binary: sop6-sessionwriter.dex
Entrypoint: sop6.SessionWriter
Size: 22,652 bytes
SHA-256: 58303723aac47a91c8a31127a99d79c57ab435ccf21fcb28a8b772495ea2e9b8

Provenance: supplied in hermes-webadb-kit, dated 2026-10-25.
The supplied kit attributes the binary to the japp.cloud client (JaecooApp,
author BK), and its analysis and vehicle test report to Hermes / David.
HABRO has not authored or modified this DEX. No source or license grant
for this binary was included in the supplied kit; this attribution does not
relicense it. Existing vendor notices apply separately to their own files.

Integration boundary
--------------------
The website runs the pinned helper only after an explicit installation
confirmation, an authorized USB ADB connection, shell uid 2000, active user 0,
and a ROM identifier containing SOP6 or SOP7. It accepts a single APK or a
compatible single-package XAPK. APK identity is read locally from the binary
AndroidManifest.xml; archive metadata does not determine package identity.
Package versions use integer comparisons without Number precision loss.

The helper has no user selector. With ordinary AOSP shell context inheritance
it targets user 0. OEM behavior and physical compatibility still need a test
on the connected vehicle. The supplied kit reports one successful SOP7 test;
this is not a hardware test performed by HABRO's web integration.

The binary was inspected statically. Its referenced methods contain no network
client, shell subprocess, root request, UID change, policy mutation or native
library load. This says nothing about the safety of a user-selected APK.

APK mode sets installFlags to 2. XAPK mode ORs its existing flags with 2 and
128. HABRO checks the real APK version against retained/installed packages
before invocation and rejects lower versions. The bit 128 does not establish
a universal installation-policy bypass; AOSP checks restrictions in the
PackageInstaller service as well as in command-line paths.

XAPK processing uses the DEX's fixed /data/local/tmp/_cust_x_extract path.
HABRO refuses a pre-existing extraction path or symlink, checks OBB destinations
for symlinks, and serializes HABRO installations across same-origin tabs via
Web Locks where available. Close other installers before using this method.
An interrupted extraction needs inspection before retrying; the web client
does not recursively remove this shared helper path.

XAPK OBB data can replace files under /sdcard/Android/obb/<package>. An OBB skip
is reported separately from APK success. No automatic uninstall, data deletion,
device-admin change, permission grant, or downgrade fallback is performed.

The helper's success line precedes XAPK OBB copying. HABRO waits for full
completion and an independent shell exit marker, rejects explicit failures,
then verifies installed version, APK count and split names for the target user.
Timeouts and disconnections after invocation are uncertain outcomes, not
successful cancellations. Normal completion cleans only the unique HABRO
upload directory; uncertain processes keep their input files. Diagnostic
collection is bounded and PID-filtered and does not clear Android log buffers.

Local validation and practical limits
------------------------------------
The website checks archive structure and binary manifest identity before USB
transfer. XAPK contents must match the supplied helper's supported layout.
ZIP64, encryption and unsupported ZIP compression are rejected. XAPK extraction
is limited to 1 GiB; individual deflated inner APKs are limited to 256 MiB for
browser memory use. Use separately extracted APKs in the standard installer
when a file is outside these limits. Android remains responsible for signature
verification and installation policy.

The first-use manual route into Carota Engineering Mode is not established by
the supplied kit. The optional activity launch requires ADB already connected.
The daily code takes the VIN's final six characters first, then extracts digits
from that fragment. Input errors remain errors; the web UI does not present
123456 as a valid calculated fallback.
